clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female with history of excessive alcohol consumption presented with progressive cerebellar ataxia manifesting as dizziness, unsteady gait, and recurrent falls over six months (including two prior hospital admissions). Physical examination revealed dysdiadochokinesis in the right hand. Laboratory studies showed anemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and elevated inflammatory markers. Brain MRI demonstrated FLAIR hyperintensity within the splenium of the corpus callosum extending to the fornix, with pericallosal white matter hyperintensity and marked cerebellar atrophy. Neuro-radiology meeting concluded these findings represented demyelination involving the splenium consistent with MBD. Treatment was initiated with vitamin B supplementation, alcohol cessation counseling, and rehabilitation referral.
